target: Build 29 release verification: Today answers only 'what does this day ask of me' — hour-grid timetable + logger + owner customization; habits live entirely on Habits (list, check-off, schedule-at-time)

customReplacement.reason: SwiftUI-only surface composed entirely from AnchorTheme tokens, Card, Chip and the existing drawn-day materials.

contract.purpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.purposeSource: PRODUCT.md; owner stated on 26 September 2026 that the product they wanted was 'a well sorted timetable and logger'
contract.canonicalPurpose: Anchor helps a person plan a realistic day, follow the current intention, and learn why the day lived differed from the day planned.
contract.driftNote: Owner then scoped the surfaces sharper on 26 September 2026: Today shows only the day's asks (timetable + logging + customize), and Habits owns the habit list plus scheduling a habit at a particular time. History stays as-is.
contract.audience: The owner using an iPhone and Mac throughout an ordinary day.
contract.job: See the day on a true time axis with nothing else competing, place or move entries by tapping open time, record what actually happened, and adjust how the grid draws itself.
contract.thesis: The plan is a straight, quiet hour grid; the day that was actually lived is drawn beside it in the hand-wiggled trace material the rest of the app uses.
contract.system: Existing paper/charcoal, native SF type, Anchor spacing, hairline hour marks, card surfaces and state tints — no new tokens.
contract.signature: Two traces on one timetable: planned blocks on the grid, and a thin drawn wiggle in the gutter marking when work really happened.
contract.risk: A full-day grid reads denser than the old compact list; mitigated by faint hairlines, an owner-adjustable day window (7–22 default), optional lived-trace, finished-entry dimming, and scroll-to-now on open.
